routes.name: Visa-free entry (exempt countries)
routes.summary: Citizens of many countries need no visa for short visits, usually 30 or 90 days. A few are per calendar year. Check the official list for your passport.

other: Stay limit depends on passport: commonly 30 or 90 days, some per calendar year
Rules can change without notice
Entry can still be refused at the border

stay.note: 30 days for some passports, 90 days for most listed ones, some per calendar year

routes.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
routes.summary: South Africa has announced an electronic travel authorisation system, but I could not confirm on an official page that it is live or who must use it. Check Home Affairs before you travel.

other: Rollout status, scope and fees not confirmed on an official page

routes.name: Airport transit
routes.summary: No transit visa is needed at O R Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports. Pakistan and Bangladesh ordinary passports still need one.

other: Transit passengers are biometrically captured
Deportees always need a transit visa

routes.name: Visitor's Visa
routes.summary: For tourism, business visits, family visits, conferences and short courses. Up to 90 days. Not issued at the border, so apply before you travel if you need a visa.

other: Passport valid 30 days past your stay with a blank page
Return or onward ticket and proof of funds
Yellow fever certificate if required

stay.note: An immigration officer sets the actual stay at entry

routes.name: Remote Work Visa (digital nomad)
routes.summary: A visa for remote workers and digital nomads was announced under 2024 regulation changes. I could not confirm the rules, income threshold or fees on an official page, so check Home Affairs.

other: Income threshold, duration and application process not confirmed on an official page

routes.name: Critical Skills Work Visa
routes.summary: For people in occupations on the Critical Skills List. Up to five years. You need a signed job offer, professional body membership and a SAQA evaluation. Not a work-seeker visa.

other: Occupation must be on the latest Critical Skills List
Professional body membership and skills confirmation, except university lecturers
Medical report and police clearance

routes.name: General Work Visa
routes.summary: For jobs where no suitably skilled South African is available. Lasts as long as the contract, up to five years. The employer has to meet several requirements.

other: Only issued where no suitable South African citizen or resident is available
Qualifications evaluated by SAQA
Employer certificates and registrations, including 60% South African staff

stay.note: Length of the contract, up to five years

routes.name: Intra-Company Transfer Work Visa
routes.summary: For moving an existing employee from a foreign branch or affiliate to South Africa. Up to four years. Cannot be renewed or extended.

other: Foreign employment contract valid at least six months
Letters from both the foreign and South African entities

routes.name: Business Visa
routes.summary: For setting up or investing in a South African business. Issued for up to three years at a time. The required capital is set by the Minister in the Gazette, and I did not find the current amount.

other: Chartered accountant certificate confirming the required investment
At least 60% of staff must be citizens or permanent residents
Capital amount set by Gazette notice, not confirmed here

routes.name: Retired Person's Visa
routes.summary: For retirees with a steady income. You need at least R37,000 a month and R37,000 net worth, as currently set. Spouse and dependent children can get visas too.

other: Medical cover
Police clearance from each country lived in 12 months or more since age 18
Amounts are set by the Minister and can change

routes.name: Financially independent permanent residence
routes.summary: Permanent residence for people who bring in a set amount of money. The amount is set by Gazette notice and I did not find it on an official page.

other: Amount set by the Minister in the Gazette, not confirmed here

routes.name: Study Visa
routes.summary: For full-time study at a South African institution. Lasts for the course period on your acceptance letter. You can work part-time up to 20 hours a week.

other: Acceptance letter from the institution
Medical cover with a South African medical scheme
Medical report and police clearance

stay.note: Tied to the course period in the acceptance letter

routes.name: Relative's Visa
routes.summary: For immediate family of a South African citizen or permanent resident. Up to two years at a time. You cannot work. Proof of R8,500 a month in support is needed, except for a spouse or dependent child.

other: Proof of relationship and sponsor's status
Financial assurance of R8,500 per person per month, not needed for spouse or dependent child
Medical report and police clearance

routes.name: Permanent residence after five years on a work visa
routes.summary: You can apply for permanent residence after holding a work visa for five continuous years. Other routes include a job offer and critical skills with five years of experience. Details and fees were not confirmed here.

other: Five continuous years on a work visa
Critical skills route needs five years post-qualification experience
Fees not confirmed

routes.name: Naturalisation
routes.summary: Citizenship for permanent residents after a set number of years. I could not read the official requirements, including years, language and dual citizenship rules.

other: Years, language and test requirements not confirmed on an official page
